summary: Private, local AI assistant that browses the web, writes and runs code, and plans multi-step tasks using models running on your own machine.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: AgenticSeek is a local alternative to cloud agents like Manus. It picks the right agent for each request: it can search and read the web and fill forms by itself, write, debug and run code in languages like Python, C, Go and Java, and break big tasks into steps across several agents. It's built to run with local reasoning models so your data stays on your device, and it can also use an API provider.
sixtySeconds.problem: Cloud agents send your files and searches to someone else's servers. AgenticSeek keeps everything on your machine.
whoFor: Privacy-minded users with a capable GPU
People who want a self-hosted agent
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a fully local setup with web browsing, coding and planning agents and a web interface.
requirements: For local models: a GPU that can run a 14B model such as Magistral, Qwen or DeepSeek

overview: Clone the repo and rename .env.example to .env, then edit it. Start a local provider such as Ollama (set OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 so Docker can reach it) and set provider_name and provider_model in config.ini; reasoning models are recommended.
Start all services in Docker with start_services full. The first start downloads images and can take up to 30 minutes; then open localhost:3000.
You can instead run with an API provider or on your own server. Voice input is in progress. It is GPL-3.0 licensed.
limitations: Needs a strong GPU for local models

steps.title: Clone and set up
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/Fosowl/agenticSeek.git
cd agenticSeek
mv .env.example .env

steps.title: Start Docker
steps.body: Launch Docker Desktop, or on Linux run sudo systemctl start docker. Check with docker info.

steps.title: Set the provider
steps.body: In config.ini set provider_name (e.g. ollama) and provider_model.

steps.title: Start services
steps.body: On Windows use start start_services.cmd full. First start can take up to 30 minutes.

firstRun.body: For example, search for something and summarize the results.
